cefrAlignment: Fits B2 (CEFR CV: can understand articles in which writers adopt particular stances and viewpoints): passages report several experts' or theories' positions, and learners follow reporting verbs (argues, concedes, doubts, dismisses) across paragraphs.
examFidelity: Matches IELTS Matching features (people, theories or groups as options, letters reusable when stated, statements paraphrased and not in passage order); I solved all 29 items independently and each has exactly one defensible option.
fixes: Practice passage 'Who travels after midnight?' was 331 words, below the B2 range of 350–550; added a neutral sentence about how the survey was carried out (now 359 words) without adding any answerable detail
learnerOutcome: A learner can anchor on names and follow each person's view across a text, separating who found, argued, conceded or rejected an idea.
